chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the death of the believer. So he said: 'The believer dies with every (type of) death — dying by drowning, and dying by being crushed (under a structure), and afflicted by predatory wild animals, and dying by thunderbolt — but it does not strike one who remembers Allah the Exalted.'

key_terms.ذَاكِر اللَّه: one who remembers God, one who is engaged in dhikr
key_terms.سَبُع: wild predatory animal — beast that kills
key_terms.صَاعِقَة: thunderbolt/lightning — a sudden violent death from the sky
key_terms.مِيتَة: manner/type of death — not just death itself but its mode or cause

ai.seo_question: What types of death can a believer die according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer narrates his question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the manner in which a believer may die. The Imam affirms that believers may die through any of a range of difficult deaths — drowning, being crushed, being attacked by beasts, or struck by lightning — yet provides a consoling exception: the thunderbolt (or perhaps any of these calamities) will not reach the one who is engaged in the remembrance (dhikr) of Allah the Exalted. This teaching contextualizes worldly trials within a framework of divine mercy for those devoted to dhikr.
